title: Questions, True/False, and Gap-Fill Exercises on Radar Speed Guns Text
summary: Activities based on a reading text about radar speed guns: comprehension questions, true/false statements about how radar guns work, and a gap-fill exercise using key words from the text such as airplane, radio waves, and speed limits.

title: Vocabulary Matching, Sentence Completion, and Writing Activity on Radar Speed Guns
summary: A continuation of exercises on the radar speed guns text, including completing sentences with missing words, matching synonyms with text vocabulary, and a writing task asking students to select and explain five interesting facts from the text.

title: Revision Exercises: Vocabulary, Modal Verbs, and Word Order
summary: A revision page with exercises on adding missing vowels to crime-related words, completing sentences with appropriate modal verbs such as must and mustn't, and rearranging jumbled words to form correct sentences using passive and causative structures.

title: Revision Exercises: Word Order, Dialogue Completion, and Sentence Equivalence
summary: Continued revision activities including rearranging words to complete sentences, filling dialogues with suggestion and offering expressions, and rewriting sentences so they have the same meaning using given modal expressions.

title: Vocabulary Exercises on Military Terms, Crime, and Security Scenarios
summary: Vocabulary practice covering military branches and roles, completing compound phrases related to security and traffic, and filling a crime report with words such as fingerprints, witness, and investigating.

title: Grammar Exercises: Modal Verbs and Suggestion Expressions
summary: Grammar practice matching sentence beginnings with appropriate endings using modals like must, needn't, and have to; selecting correct should/shouldn't options; and completing dialogues with expressions like shall, could, and let's.

title: Writing Sentences with Modal Verbs and Causative Verbs Exercises
summary: Practice writing original sentences with have to, mustn't, and don't have to, followed by a rewrite exercise using the causative forms get, have, and make in sentences describing someone else performing an action.

title: Writing Task: Advice Letter to Ahmed About a Security Guard Interview
summary: A guided writing task requiring a 100–120 word letter advising Ahmed on attending a security job interview, using you should and you shouldn't at least five times, with separate paragraphs for travel advice and interview etiquette.
